sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Define the minimum document set and core fields required for a patient case review.

sections.heading: Required documents
sections.text: Every case must contain: (1) Patient Registration Form, (2) Attending Physician Note, (3) Discharge Summary, and (4) Claim Submission Form.

sections.heading: Required claim fields
sections.text: The Claim Submission Form must include patient identity, admission date, discharge date, primary diagnosis, attending physician, and physician signature.

sections.heading: Procedure-specific support
sections.text: If the claim includes a procedure listed in SOP-05, the corresponding supporting report is also required.

sections.heading: Review action
sections.text: A missing required core document, required claim field, or required procedure-support document must be flagged for review. Do not infer missing content from another document.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Ensure all documents belong to the same patient.

sections.heading: Exact identifiers
sections.text: Patient ID and date of birth must match across the case documents.

sections.heading: Names
sections.text: Names may be normalized for case, spacing, punctuation, and common title differences. A name difference alone should not automatically be treated as a mismatch if Patient ID and DOB agree.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: Any Patient ID or DOB mismatch is a high-severity issue and requires human review.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Guide comparison of diagnoses across physician notes, discharge summaries, and claim forms.

sections.heading: Semantic equivalence
sections.text: Equivalent terminology and standard abbreviations should not be flagged as conflicts. Example: “Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications” and “T2DM, uncomplicated” are equivalent for this review.

sections.heading: True conflict
sections.text: Different clinical conditions should be flagged when the claim diagnosis contradicts the final documented diagnosis. Example: “Pneumonia” and “Acute bronchitis” are not treated as equivalent.

sections.heading: Uncertainty
sections.text: A suspected, possible, rule-out, or not-confirmed diagnosis must not be treated as a confirmed diagnosis. If a claim asserts a confirmed diagnosis while the clinical record remains uncertain, escalate for human review.

sections.heading: AI behavior
sections.text: The assistant should cite the documents used to make the comparison and should not silently rewrite diagnoses.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Validate basic chronological consistency.

sections.heading: Admission/discharge rule
sections.text: Discharge date must be the same as or later than the admission date.

sections.heading: Procedure date rule
sections.text: Any procedure date must fall within the documented admission-to-discharge period unless a supporting note explicitly explains otherwise.

sections.heading: Severity
sections.text: A discharge date before admission is a high-severity issue and requires review.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Define required evidence for selected procedures.

sections.heading: Colonoscopy
sections.text: Requires an Endoscopy Report documenting procedure date, findings, and conclusion/impression.

sections.heading: CT abdomen with contrast
sections.text: Requires a Radiology Report containing at least Study Date, Findings, and Impression.

sections.heading: Appendectomy
sections.text: Requires an Operative Report containing procedure date, operative findings, and surgeon identification.

sections.heading: Missing report
sections.text: If a required procedure report is absent, flag as high severity.

sections.heading: Incomplete report
sections.text: If a required report exists but a required section is blank or clearly incomplete, flag for human review. Do not invent the missing section.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Define when the AI assistant must defer to a human reviewer.

sections.heading: Mandatory escalation
sections.text: Escalate when there is conflicting clinical evidence, uncertain diagnosis status, incomplete supporting evidence, identity mismatch, or a rule outcome cannot be determined confidently.

sections.heading: Decision boundary
sections.text: The AI assistant may identify issues and summarize evidence. It must not autonomously approve, reject, or deny a claim.

sections.heading: Uncertainty
sections.text: When evidence is insufficient, the correct output is “needs_review” with a clear reason, not a guessed conclusion.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Ensure every AI-generated issue can be traced back to source documents.

sections.heading: Evidence requirement
sections.text: Every reported issue must identify the source document and the relevant field, section, or quoted value used as evidence.

sections.heading: No unsupported claims
sections.text: The assistant must distinguish documented facts from hypotheses and must not fabricate missing values.

sections.heading: Audit trail
sections.text: A production design should preserve case ID, input document references, rule or model version, output, and review outcome for later audit.
